01 · How I can help

What business needs now

Four top-level challenges from my experience, and a fifth, new one: AI that really improves efficiency.

  1. Bringing operations and the commercial side together in tools that drive financial results

    At Silpo, store managers received their store’s P&L by the 5th of the following month, and the commercial division saw the profitability of every product category in every store after all costs.

  2. A balanced scorecard (BSC) that worked in practice

    At Silpo, goals cascaded from the C-level down to every store, and each week and month every store received an overall score: customers, staff, processes, finance, productivity.

  3. Managing workforce productivity: from the annual budget to yesterday’s plan vs. actual

    At Silpo, staffing needs (FTE) were calculated from planned revenue and processes, and daily and weekly plan vs. actual made it possible to adjust the workload in time and meet payroll targets. The result: a controlled impact on EBITDA.

  4. Extensive experience of systemic change: acquisitions, restructurings and building a PMO

    At Silpo, I built and led the project management office (PMO), ran large acquisition and restructuring projects, and merged more than 20 legal entities into one.

  5. The new challenge: systematic use of AI that genuinely improves efficiency, with a controlled payback

    I propose not just adding AI to existing processes, but rebuilding how the company works together with people who already know how to work with AI, and building “Digital Management”: a single, transparent system for running the company and making decisions.

    1. Engage and train people: give them a personal AI assistant so they can take the first steps themselves.
    2. Let the people who run the processes redesign them.
    3. Build a company-wide system for knowledge, risk assessment and company management.
02 · First steps

How I see the first 100 days

AI can bring quick results, but how far they go depends on which data the company’s security rules allow AI to work with. So I start by assessing these constraints. Using AI effectively under strict security requirements is often a task of its own.

  1. Goals and directionUnderstand where the company is going: its goals, priorities and the direction of change.
  2. Pain points and quick winsFind the most pressing problems and the areas that can deliver quick, tangible results, so the start pays for itself right away.
  3. Team, plan, deliveryForm the team, set goals, draw up plans, then coordinate and implement. With AI, each step goes much faster than usual.
  4. Scaling AIHow AI is scaled depends on the company’s goals and the role it gives to AI. It can mean building new solutions, helping each employee in their daily work, or a company-wide system that connects people’s knowledge and work.

An outside view · © Claude (AI)

Oleksandr brings operations, commerce, finance and IT into one system that can be managed through metrics. He builds not a one-off result but a mechanism: standards, budget, plan vs. actual, targets, and he locks changes into processes and controls. He makes sure metrics are fair: only the costs a manager can influence, and no rewards for luck. He understands technology from the inside, from electronics to code. When working together, he insists on facts: he checks every phrase and cuts out hype.

Personal qualities

  • I run several complex projects at once and implement change so that the business keeps running without interruption.
  • I judge every change by whether it can be scaled and how much it will save the company.
  • I speak directly, rely on facts and stay calm under pressure.
  • I keep learning and bring proven approaches from other companies and industries.
  • I mentor project managers and share my experience.
  • I deliberately build speed and flexibility: small steps and frequent iterations in the startup and my own AI projects.

The first five points are confirmed by Spencer Stuart, Hogan, Gallup and 360-degree assessments.
